land.text: 'the islands of Upolu, Savai'i, Apolima and Manono'

predecessors.note: 'In 1899 after the Second Samoan Civil War, the Samoan Islands were divided by the three involved powers'; Tripartite Convention signed at Washington on 2 December 1899, ratifications exchanged 16 February 1900. The kingdom-of-samoa dossier ends 1900-02 with counterpart german-empire.

land.text: German Samoa, which New Zealand 'occupied ... through to 1920' and governed 'as a League of Nations Class C Mandate'

successors.note: New Zealand occupied it from 29 August 1914; the Class C mandate was conferred on 17 December 1920 (infobox 'League mandate: 17 December 1920'); independent as Western Samoa in 1962 (new-zealand dossier, oc-02-a; no 'samoa' dossier exists yet).

correction.text: the German part of the partitioned archipelago: 'the islands of Upolu, Savai'i, Apolima and Manono' (the eastern islands, Tutuila, went to the United States)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the country Samoa, cells: 9 (about 2276 km2), against the page's 2,831 km2 for 1912 (ratio about 0.8; the grid cannot show the small islands). American Samoa, east of 171 W, is not in the shape. Held to 1920 as the owner's shape: New Zealand occupies it from 29 August 1914 (occupation event, hatched).

ledger.note: 1900: Germany raises its flag over Samoa (1 March 1900): the colonial period 'officially began with the raising of the imperial flag on 1 March 1900', after the Tripartite Convention (signed 2 December 1899, ratified 16 February 1900) divided the Samoan Islands; 'consisting of the islands of Upolu, Savai'i, Apolima and Manono'.
1914: New Zealand occupies German Samoa: the colony 'was invaded unopposed on the morning of 29 August 1914 by troops of the Samoa Expeditionary Force' (infobox 'NZ occupation: 30 August 1914').
1920: the occupation becomes a mandate: infobox 'League mandate: 17 December 1920'; New Zealand governed the islands 'as a League of Nations Class C Mandate'.
1920: New Zealand receives the Class C mandate over the former German colony (17 December 1920).

region.text: German Samoa as it stood in 1914

ledger.note: 1920: German Samoa ends as a state with the mandate. The lead says it 'was a German protectorate from 1900 to 1920' and the Treaty of Versailles date is 10 January 1920 (infobox); December 1920 is the mandate, the date the New Zealand dossier uses.

wars.name: New Zealand occupation of German Samoa (First World War)
wars.outcome: 'invaded unopposed on the morning of 29 August 1914'; held under New Zealand occupation to the mandate of 17 December 1920.
wars.note: No fighting is described on the page.

certainty.note: An island group fixed by the Tripartite Convention of 1899 (the line between German and American Samoa); the border is the sea.

sources.title: German Samoa
sources.note: Flag raised 1 March 1900, Tripartite Convention 2 December 1899 (ratified 16 February 1900), four islands, capital Apia, NZ invasion 29 August 1914, mandate 17 December 1920, area 2,831 km2.

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. One page opened (German Samoa); the Tripartite Convention date differs from the 14 November 1899 given by the British Solomon Islands infobox (that page gives the Samoa convention as 14 November 1899, this one 2 December 1899 signed, 16 February 1900 ratified).
The page gives no single end date: 'a German protectorate from 1900 to 1920' with the mandate on 17 December 1920 is the dossier's end. new-zealand (oc-02-a) records the occupation_start (August 1914) and occupation_end/gain (December 1920) with counterpart german-samoa, which this dossier mirrors; its 1962 independence and a 'samoa' dossier are the oc-02-a / oc-02-b side. kingdom-of-samoa (oc-01) ends 1900-02 with counterpart german-empire; this dossier is the state that holds the land from 1 March 1900. American Samoa is not covered. The Second Samoan Civil War appears on the page only as 1899 context.
